MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
The following standards will go into effect on July 1, 2021.
The content areas covered by the social studies standards
When a district incorporates or integrates social studies
content into district curriculum or offers a course in social
studies, the following skills at each grade level may apply
compare and evaluate sources for relevance, perspective, and accuracy
use sources to gather evidence to develop and refine claims

MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR
The civics and government content standards for kindergarten are that each student will
recognize the people who create and carry out rules for the school and classroom
define that being a citizen of the classroom and school community means following established rules and expectations
demonstrate citizenship through their interactions in the classroom and school community
The economics content standards for kindergarten are that each student will
explain and identify examples of goods and services
describe goods and products that are produced in local regions
The geography content standard for kindergarten is that each student will use maps, and other representations, to describe place characteristics
The history content standard for kindergarten is that each student will distinguish between past, present, and future time

MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR FIRST GRADE
The civics and government content standards for first grade are that each student will
demonstrate being a citizen of a classroom and school community through interactions and by following established rules and expectations
recognize the people, and their roles, who create and carry out rules for the school and classroom
The economics content standards for first grade are that each student will
explain the difference between needs and wants
describe goods and products that are produced in local regions
The geography content standards for first grade are that each student will
identify and describe human and physical local landmarks
construct maps and other representations of familiar places
The history content standards for first grade are that each student will
distinguish between past, present, and future time
understand how events might be described differently depending on historical contexts and perspectives, including those of tribes in Montana
Document Created April 5, 2021 | Effective date July 1, 2021 | opi.mt.gov | Page 4
MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SECOND GRADE
The civics and government content standards for second grade are that each student will
explain the roles of people who help govern different communities including tribal communities
demonstrate ways to show good citizenship in the classroom, school, and community
The economics content standards for second grade are that each student will
describe the goods and services that people in the local, state, and national community produce
describe examples of the goods and services that governments provide
identify resources people use to access the goods and services they want and need
The geography content standards for second grade are that each student will
use the basic components of a map to identify physical and political features, including American Indian reservations
describe how geography and human activities impact each other
The history content standards for second grade are that each student will
identify how people lived differently in the past than they do today
understand that there are twelve distinct and unique tribes within Montana whose people contribute to modern life
identify different kinds of historical sources, including oral histories of American Indians
Document Created April 5, 2021 | Effective date July 1, 2021 | opi.mt.gov | Page 5
MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR THIRD GRADE
The civics and government content standards for third grade are that each student will
describe and identify the basic functions of local government, including tribal governments
recognize that civic participation involves remaining accurately informed about public issues, taking action, and voting in elections
The economics content standards for third grade are that each student will
compare the benefits and costs of individual choices
identify examples of human and natural resources that are used to produce goods and services
explain economic interdependence within historical and contemporary contexts
The geography content standards for third grade are that each student will
examine maps and other representations to identify historical and contemporary political and cultural patterns in the Americas
identify environmental and technological events and conditions and how humans and the environment impact each other
identify landforms and other physical characteristics of the Americas
The history content standards for third grade are that each student will
identify tribes in Montana by their original and current names
explain how perspective impacts the telling of historical events
Document Created April 5, 2021 | Effective date July 1, 2021 | opi.mt.gov | Page 6
MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR FOURTH
The civics and government content standards for fourth grade are that each student will
demonstrate civic participation within the classroom or school
practice deliberative processes when making decisions as a group
describe how rules, laws, and policies are implemented by local, state, national, and tribal governments
define sovereignty for tribes in Montana
identify key foundational documents in Montana's government
The economics content standards for fourth grade are that each student will
identify the various pressures and incentives that influence the decisions people make in short-term and long-term situations
identify basic elements of Montana's state economic system including agriculture, business, natural resources, and labor
identify various resources and labor that are used to provide goods and services in Montana
explain how trade leads to increasing economic interdependence among groups in Montana
The geography content standards for fourth grade are that each student will
examine maps and other representations to explain the movement of people
identify and label the tribes in Montana and their indigenous territories, and current locations
investigate the physical, political, and cultural characteristics of places, regions, and people in Montana
analyze environmental and technological events and conditions and how humans and the environment impact each other with relation to settlements and migration in Montana
Document Created April 5, 2021 | Effective date July 1, 2021 | opi.mt.gov | Page 7
MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR FOURTH
The history content standards for fourth grade are that each student will
understand tribes in Montana have their own unique histories
identify events and policies that have impacted and been influenced by tribes in Montana
explain how Montana has changed over time given its cultural diversity and how this history impacts the present
describe how historical accounts are impacted by individual perspectives

MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR FIFTH GRADE
The civics and government content standards for fifth grade are that each student will
examine the diverse origins, ideals, and purposes of rules, laws, and key United States constitutional provisions and other foundational documents
use deliberative processes when engaging in civic participation within the classroom or school
distinguish between the responsibilities of local, state, tribal, and national governments
explain how democracy relies upon active and responsible participation of citizens
describe the basic duties of the three branches of government
The economics content standards for fifth grade are that each student will
explain how people have to make choices between wants and needs and evaluate the outcomes or consequences of those choices
identify positive and negative incentives that influence the decisions people make
identify resources and labor that are used to produce goods and services
explain the role of money in the exchange of goods and services
describe the role of manufacturing and agriculture in the economy of the United States
describe how interest rates impact economic decision making
The geography content standards for fifth grade are that each student will
identify and label US regions, territories, states and their capitals/major cities
create, organize, and present geographic information to show settlement patterns in the United States, including impacts on tribal lands
analyze environmental and technological events and conditions and how humans and the environment impact each other with relation to settlements and migration
The history content standards for fifth grade are that each student will

identify roles of individuals and groups and their impact on United States and tribal historical events
understand the unique historical perspectives of American Indians
analyze historical documents and their impact on tribes in Montana and their sovereignty

MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SIXTH
The civics and government content standards for sixth through eighth grade are that each student will
explain a variety of forms of government from the past or present
explain the structure of and key principles in foundational documents, including the Montana Constitution
explain how global and American Indian civilizations and governments have contributed to foundational documents of the United States
distinguish the structure, organization, powers, and limits of government at the local, state, national, and tribal levels
identify events and leaders that ensure that key United States principles of equality and civil rights are applied to various groups, including American Indians
demonstrate that the United States government includes concepts of both a democracy and a republic
employ strategies for civic involvement that address a state or local, or national issues
The economics content standards for sixth through eighth grade are that each student will
explain how economic decisions impact individuals, businesses, and society, including Indigenous societies
analyze examples of how groups and individuals have considered profit and personal values in making economic choices in the past and/or present
explain the roles of producers and consumers in market systems
describe the role of competition in the determination of prices and wages in a market economy
explain ways in which money facilitates exchange and impacts transactional costs
Document Created April 5, 2021 | Effective date July 1, 2021 | opi.mt.gov | Page 11
MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SIXTH
explain how changes in supply, demand, and labor standards cause changes in prices and quantities of goods, services, and other capital
The geography content standards for sixth through eighth grade are that each student will
construct and analyze maps using scale, direction, symbols, legends, and projections to gather information about regions across the world
identify the location of places and regions in the world and understand their physical, political, and cultural characteristics
analyze maps and charts from a specific time period to understand an issue or event
explain how the environment and geographic features have affected people and how people have affected the environment throughout Montana, the United States, and the world
explain the role and impact of spatial patterns of settlement and movement in shaping societies and cultures, including Indigenous cultures
identify how the historical and contemporary movement of people, goods, and ideas from one area can impact change, conflict, and cooperation in other areas
identify the cultural roots of major world regions
The history content standards for sixth through eighth grade are that each student will
explore complex civilizations, and identify elements of change and continuity across historical eras in Montana, the Americas, and world history
analyze how the historical events relate to one another and are shaped by historical context, including societies in the Americas
analyze how, since European contact, historical events and policies have mutually impacted American Indian and European societies

THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SIXTH
identify how new archaeological and scientific information shapes historical understanding
explain how Montana has changed over time and how this history impacts the present
understand that there are multiple perspectives and interpretations of historical events
analyze how people's perspectives shaped the historical narratives they created
identify limitations and biases in primary and secondary sources, specifically regarding misinformation and stereotypes
understand that the questions people ask shape the conclusions they reach

MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR NINTH
The civics and government content standards for ninth through twelfth grade are that each student will

analyze and evaluate the ideas and principles contained in the foundational documents of the United States, and explain how they establish a system of government that has powers, responsibilities, and limits
analyze the impact of constitutions, laws, treaties, and international agreements on the maintenance of domestic and international relationships
evaluate the impact of international agreements on contemporary world issues
apply civic virtues and democratic principles when working with others
evaluate how citizens and institutions address social and political problems at the local, state, tribal, national, and/or international levels
evaluate the American governmental system compared to international governmental systems
explain the foundations and complexity of sovereignty for federally recognized tribes in Montana
evaluate appropriate deliberative processes in multiple settings
evaluate government procedures for making decisions at the local, state, national, tribal, and international levels
analyze historical, contemporary, and emerging means of changing societies, promoting the common good, and protecting rights

analyze the impact and roles of personal interests and perspectives, market, media, and group influences on the application of civic virtues, democratic principles, constitutional rights, and human rights
evaluate citizens' and institutions' effectiveness in ensuring civil rights at the local, state, tribal, national, and international levels
Document Created April 5, 2021 | Effective date July 1, 2021 | opi.mt.gov | Page 14
MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR NINTH
The economics content standards for ninth through twelfth grade are that each student will
analyze how pressures and incentives impact economic choices and their costs and benefits for different groups, including American Indians
explain how economic cycles affect personal financial decisions
analyze the ways in which pressures and incentives influence what is produced and distributed in a market system
evaluate the extent to which competition among producers, among consumers, and among laborers exists in specific markets
describe the consequences of competition in specific markets
evaluate benefits, costs, and possible outcomes of government policies to influence market outcomes
use current data to explain the influence of changes in spending, production, and the money supply on various economic conditions
use economic indicators to analyze the current and future state of the economy
evaluate the selection of monetary and fiscal policies in a variety of economic conditions
The geography content standards for ninth through twelfth grade are that each student will
use geospatial reasoning to create maps to display and explain the spatial patterns of cultural and environmental characteristics
use geographic data to analyze variations in the spatial patterns of cultural and environmental characteristics at multiple scales
use maps, satellite images, photographs, and other representations to explain relationships between the locations of places and regions and their political, cultural, and economic dynamics
analyze relationships and interactions within and between human and physical systems to explain reciprocal influences that occur among them, including American Indians

MONTANA CONTENT STANDARDS FOR SOCIAL STUDIES FOR K-12
THE SOCIAL STUDIES CONTENT STANDARDS FOR NINTH
evaluate the impact of human settlement activities on the environmental, political, and cultural characteristics of specific places and regions
analyze the role of geography on interactions and conflicts between various cultures in Montana, the United States, and the world
evaluate the influence of long-term climate variability on human migration and settlement patterns, resource use, and land uses at local-to-global scales
evaluate the consequences of human-driven and natural catastrophes on global trade, politics, and human migration
The history content standards for ninth through twelfth grade are that each student will
analyze how unique circumstances of time, place, and historical contexts shape individuals' lives
analyze change and continuity in historical eras in US and world history
identify ways in which people and groups exercise agency in difficult historical, contemporary, and tribal contexts
analyze multiple, and complex causal factors that have shaped major events in US and world history, including American Indian history
explain events in relation to both their intended and unintended consequences, including governmental policies impacting American Indians
distinguish between long-term causes and triggering events in developing a historical argument
analyze how historical, cultural, social, political, ideological, and economic contexts shape people's perspectives
analyze the ways in which the perspectives of those writing history shaped the history they produced
evaluate how historiography is influenced by perspective and available historical sources

access, synthesize, and evaluate information to communicate and apply social studies knowledge to real world situations
analyze how people create and change structures of power, authority, and governance to understand the operation of government and to demonstrate civic responsibility
apply geographic knowledge and skills (e.g., location, place, human/environment interactions, movement, and regions)
compare and evaluate sources for relevance, perspective, and accuracy
demonstrate an understanding of the effects of time, continuity, and change on historical and future perspectives and relationships
use sources to gather evidence to develop and refine claims
make informed decisions based on an understanding of the economic principles of production, distribution, exchange, and consumption
demonstrate an understanding of the impact of human interaction and cultural diversity on societies
